summary.headline: Royal Orchid Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 34% to ₹116 crore and EBITDA 53% to ₹31.66 crore, with PBT lifted by a Tanzania exceptional gain.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 34% YoY to ₹116 crore (from ₹86.77 crore) and EBITDA grew about 53% to ₹31.66 crore (from ₹20.79 crore). Reported profit includes an exceptional gain from the displacement of the Tanzania subsidiary, and management says the focus remains on recurring earnings. The company opened 5 hotels adding 426 rooms in the period, taking the operating portfolio to 127 hotels, with Hotel Iconica Mumbai posting its first positive EBITDA in the quarter. Management said bottom-line flow-through is still weak and attributed part of the pressure to GST input credit disallowance (about ₹2 crore per quarter) and pre-opening costs for a Vadodara hotel.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated PBT before exceptional items (Q2 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: vs EBITDA loss of ₹1.4 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Managed hotels
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 11.5% YoY in Q2; management cited operating (pre-tax) margin of about 37-38%, or about 36% after the 5% royalty paid to the parent, and 42-43% before intercompany adjustment (as clarified on the call). Managed hotels average about 59% occupancy at ADR near ₹4,000.

segments.name: Hotel Iconica, Mumbai
segments.commentary: Revenue of about ₹20 crore in Q2 versus ₹3 crore a year earlier, with ADR up from about ₹7,800 to ₹8,000 and occupancy about 70% (versus 17% a year earlier). Top line has run at about ₹21 crore for the last two quarters; the ₹25 crore per quarter breakeven level was discussed, with the Q4 FY27 target to beat Q4 FY26's ₹23 crore.

segments.name: Asset-light/managed growth pipeline
segments.commentary: Over 50 upcoming properties expected to add more than 3,500 rooms; about 30 hotels with roughly 1,800 keys expected to open in the next 12 months.

guidance_outlook: Managed hotel growth expected to be double-digit and faster than 10-15% from next year, though not guided precisely; no revenue targets given.
About 30 hotels (~1,800 keys) expected to open in the next 12 months; development team being ramped up.
Iconica expected to hit ₹25 crore quarterly revenue at some point; management hopes to achieve it in FY27 (Q4 is seasonally strongest).
Other expenses expected to stay in the ₹33-35 crore per quarter range for the year.
Management expects bottom-line ratios to improve from the second year of Iconica onwards; GST relief from government discussions possibly from January.
capex_capacity: Portfolio at 127 operating hotels; 5 hotels (426 rooms) opened in the quarter.
Pipeline of over 50 properties and 3,500+ rooms; asset-light model with revenue-share and lease structures.
Newly opened managed hotels take about six months to stabilise; older hotels about one year.
Vadodara hotel opened on revenue-share basis with pre-opening cost of about ₹1-1.5 crore hitting the quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 occupancy about 70% for both Iconica and the managed portfolio; management noted marginally higher occupancy so far in Q3 with no holidays until mid-December.
Q2 seasonality: monsoon (July-September) weighs on Q1-Q2; Q3-Q4 are seasonally stronger. Iconica Q1 FY27 was hit by a sharp drop in inbound Mumbai traffic after the April conflict, per management.
Premiumisation: Iconica is the first step; Bengaluru resort ADR cited as rising from ₹80 lakh to ₹2 crore in value terms from investments (as stated).
Mid-market portfolio of 100+ hotels with ADR around ₹5,000; most managed hotels are mid-market and most owned hotels are below ₹7,500 ADR, so GST input credit disallowance hits them.

qa_highlights.question: What is the managed-hotel growth trajectory for this year and the next three to four years, and what were PBT margins in Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be double-digit and higher than the 10-15% range from next year as about 30 hotels open; no revenue guidance given. Q2 managed hotel revenue grew about 11.5%; operating margin about 37-38% pre-tax (about 36% after the 5% royalty, 42-43% before intercompany adjustment). Prior-year margin was not stated.

qa_highlights.question: When will Iconica reach about ₹25 crore quarterly top line, given it has run at about ₹21 crore for two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel only got full licensing at end-November last year, so Q2 FY27 is effectively its fourth full quarter; Q4 is the strongest quarter, with the aspiration to beat Q4 FY26's ₹23 crore and hit ₹25 crore this financial year.

qa_highlights.question: When is the inflection point on the bottom line, given heavy upfront costs and the ROCE target of about 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a 2030 long-term scale goal, said Iconica is only in its first year, and expects ratios to improve from its second year. It cited GST input credit disallowance costing about ₹2 crore per quarter, with government representations pending and possible relief from January.

qa_highlights.question: What is Iconica's occupancy and ARR trend, and why did margin decline sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 occupancy about 70% versus 17% a year earlier; ADR up from ~₹7,800 to ~₹8,000; revenue up from ₹3 crore to ₹20 crore; EBITDA from a loss of ₹1.4 crore to +₹30 lakh. Sequential margin pressure attributed to seasonality and the Vadodara pre-opening cost of about ₹1-1.5 crore. Management said the Q1 to Q2 occupancy comparison should be read like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue growth from existing hotels be separated from newly opened hotels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the investor presentation (slide 27) has ADR and occupancy by owned and managed hotels; managed hotels average about 59% occupancy at about ₹4,000 ADR. Management also noted the company operates 127 hotels excluding the signed pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will other expenses stay around ₹32-33 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management expects other expenses in the ₹33-35 crore range per quarter for the year, with no major one-offs expected after an earlier reclassification to P&L.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the NCLT matter involving Shir Saga Developers and any financial exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the NCLT dispute is between the company and its partner, is a control issue rather than financial, and carries no financial implication even on outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate governance concerns: audit qualifications, SEBI order and related-party loans.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a SEBI accounting point is pending with a final hearing held and an order expected soon, with no expected financial impact; the audit qualification relates to a case the company is defending and is outside its control.

risks_watch: Bottom-line flow-through remains weak despite revenue growth; the company itself says the inflection point depends on Iconica settling down.
GST input credit disallowance (about ₹2 crore per quarter) on revenue-share and lease models for mid-market hotels; relief uncertain, possibly from January.
Iconica needs to reach about ₹25 crore quarterly revenue to clearly break even; Q4 seasonality is key.
Pending SEBI accounting matter and audit qualifications; NCLT dispute with partner (Shir Saga) on control.
Managed hotel growth depends on partner development timelines for about 30 hotels in 12 months.
Management declined to give managed-hotel revenue targets, limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and pipeline, defensive on profitability and governance. Management acknowledged slow bottom-line flow-through and repeatedly deflected to 'the first year of Iconica' and external factors (GST, war-related traffic, monsoon). Specific numbers were given on Iconica and margins, but there was no quantitative guidance on managed revenue or the inflection timing.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bottom-line flow-through remains weak (PBT before exceptionals ₹5.57 crore), Iconica has run at ~₹21 crore for two quarters versus a ₹25 crore target, and GST disallowance of ~₹2 crore per quarter depends on uncertain government relief.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Premiumisation via Iconica is the first step and a Bengaluru resort is cited, but no specific new brand or product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Iconica reaches ₹25 crore quarterly revenue and breakeven
rows.why: Iconica has run at ~₹21 crore for two quarters and ₹25 crore per quarter is the breakeven level; management aspires to hit it in Q4 FY27 (Q4 FY26 was ₹23 crore), but it is not firmly guided.

rows.label: GST input credit disallowance relief
rows.why: GST disallowance costs about ₹2 crore per quarter on mid-market revenue-share and lease hotels (ADR ~₹5,000); management has government representations pending with relief possibly from January.

rows.label: Other expenses held at ₹33-35 crore per quarter
rows.why: Management guided other expenses to stay in the ₹33-35 crore range per quarter for the year, with no major one-offs expected after the reclassification.

tone.note: Management was confident on the hotel pipeline and Iconica's occupancy and ADR gains, but defensive on profitability, GST, and governance matters (SEBI order, NCLT dispute, audit qualifications); analysts pressed on the bottom-line inflection point and the timing of Iconica's breakeven.
